answer: Give each agent identity a maturation clock: new identities start with zero economic weight and earn full rights only after 30 days of steady, verifiable activity. A sybil farmer must keep thousands of clones alive and working for a full month before any can claim rewards, turning a cheap one-day flood into a month of rented compute and constant upkeep. The check is on-chain: each identity's activity log hashes into its kernel record, and only logs crossing the age threshold climb to the summit of full rights; the rest stay in the meadow of limited access.
